skill.name: env-and-assets-bootstrap
skill.description: Environment and assets sub-skill for README-first AI repo reproduction. Use when the task is specifically to prepare a conservative conda-first environment, checkpoint and dataset path assumptions, cache location hints, and setup notes before any run on a README-documented repository. Do not use for repo scanning, full orchestration, paper interpretation, final run reporting, or generic environment setup that is not tied to a specific reproduction target.
skill.summary: Prepares conservative environment and asset assumptions for README-first AI reproduction work.
skill.author: lllllllama

security_audit.summary: Most static detections are false positives caused by markdown backticks, shell wrapper path discovery, and policy prose. The confirmed issue is scripts/bootstrap_env.py executing conda, mamba, virtualenv, and pip commands against a target repository. This behavior is expected for setup, but it is risky for untrusted repositories because package installation can run code.

remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before running installs, and keep dry-run guidance prominent for first use.

remediation.issue: Target repository setup files can execute code during installation
remediation.suggestion: Add a preflight review that lists detected setup files and warns before pip or editable installs.

content.value_statement: Research repositories often have unclear setup and asset paths. This skill turns README evidence into conservative environment commands and asset assumptions before runs.
actual_capabilities: Plans conda-first or virtualenv setup from README evidence and top-level environment files.
Detects environment.yml, requirements.txt, pyproject.toml, and setup.py files.
Bootstraps environments with conda, mamba, or virtualenv when requested.
Creates an asset manifest for datasets, checkpoints, cache directories, and model files.
Reports unresolved setup and asset risks for reproduction work.
limitations: It does not verify package safety or dependency provenance.
It does not download assets automatically.
It relies on repository documentation and simple file detection.
It is scoped to README-documented AI repo reproduction, not general development setup.

use_cases.title: Prepare a paper reproduction
use_cases.description: Create conservative setup notes before running a selected AI research repository.

use_cases.title: Review environment risk
use_cases.description: Identify setup files, package-manager choices, and unresolved dependency questions before installation.

use_cases.title: Create asset path notes
use_cases.description: Map expected datasets, checkpoints, cache folders, and missing asset sources for a reproduction task.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Setup From README
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill on the selected repository. Summarize the safest environment path and asset assumptions before any run.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare Missing Asset Notes
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the repository documentation and list expected checkpoints, datasets, cache paths, and unresolved asset risks.

prompt_templates.title: Bootstrap With Dry Run
prompt_templates.prompt: For this repository, propose the conda-first bootstrap plan and explain what the dry-run execution would change.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Cross-Platform Setup
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare Linux, macOS, and Windows setup constraints for this target repository, then produce a conservative execution plan.

output_examples.input: A repository has a documented conda environment file and checkpoint paths in the README.
output_examples.output: The skill recommends using the documented conda environment, preserving the declared environment name, and recording checkpoint paths as required assets.

output_examples.input: A repository has only requirements metadata and no documented datasets.
output_examples.output: The skill proposes a virtualenv fallback, marks dataset sources as unresolved, and separates inferred paths from confirmed README evidence.

output_examples.input: A reproduction target needs setup review before running any command.
output_examples.output: The skill produces setup notes, package-manager assumptions, asset path risks, and dry-run guidance for user approval.

best_practices: Run the bootstrap in dry-run mode before installing dependencies.
Use documented README sources before inferring packages or assets.
Record unresolved versions, missing files, and assumed paths in the final report.
anti_patterns: Running package installs from an unknown repository without reviewing setup files.
Replacing documented constraints with broad dependency upgrades.
Treating inferred checkpoint or dataset paths as confirmed sources.

faq.question: Does this skill run experiments?
faq.answer: No. It prepares environment and asset assumptions before a reproduction run.

faq.question: Can it use conda and mamba?
faq.answer: Yes. The bootstrapper can use conda or mamba when they are available.

faq.question: Does it install packages automatically?
faq.answer: It can execute installs when requested. Use dry-run mode first for untrusted repositories.

faq.question: Does it download datasets or checkpoints?
faq.answer: No. It creates asset manifests and records source hints, but it does not download assets.

faq.question: Is it useful outside AI paper reproduction?
faq.answer: Only in limited cases. The skill is designed for README-documented AI reproduction targets.

faq.question: What should users review before running it?
faq.answer: Users should review setup files, package sources, target paths, and any install commands.
